Forecast run: Sun, Nov 1, 4:10 PM (the page refreshes this a few times a day).
Each hour: time, direction and speed (knots, g = gust), odds of 12kt or more, regime, waves, tide height in ft with r rising or f falling. OUTFLOW NOT RIDDEN = Squamish outflow, never recommend. OFF DIR = direction does not work at that spot.
Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Sun, Nov 1 7:26am to 6:25pm; Mon, Nov 2 7:28am to 6:23pm; Tue, Nov 3 7:30am to 6:22pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Sun, Nov 1 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Outflow morning, and Pam Rocks is ahead of the page. It read NNE 25 gusting 29 at 6am after 28 to 29 overnight. Pemberton is 2.5 hPa above Vancouver and holding, and Environment Canada has a gale warning for Howe Sound: northerly 20 to 30, easing to 15 early this afternoon. The page drops Porteau to 11 by 8am, but I think it holds longer.

My pick is Porteau from first light (7:26am) to about 9:30am, NNE 20 to 25 with 3ft of swell early. Go early: the tide floods from 5.8ft at 7am to a 15.5ft high at 12:46pm, which may flatten the swell as it fills. If Pam Rocks drops under 22 it's done.

Everywhere else is light. Sand Heads has NNW 13, offshore for Boundary Bay, and Point Atkinson is E 3. Squamish is an outflow, so boat only.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 PM PCT 01 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Monday. Gale warning in effect. Wind light increasing to northerly outflow 15 knots this evening and to northerly outflow 25 to 35 after midnight. Wind diminishing to northerly outflow 15 to 20 near noon Monday.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 PM PCT 01 November 2026): Tonight and Monday. Wind light becoming southeast 10 knots late this evening then becoming light early Monday afternoon.

Track record, last 30 days: Porteau Cove (scored at Pam Rocks): typical miss 3.31kt, caught 74% of windy hours, 13% false alarms; Steveston - Garry Point Park (scored at Sand Heads): typical miss 2.54kt, caught 78% of windy hours, 19% false alarms; Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal Causeway (scored at Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal): typical miss 2.69kt, caught 57% of windy hours, 18% false alarms; Erwin Park (scored at Point Atkinson): typical miss 2.89kt, caught 35% of windy hours, 34% false alarms. Other spots are not measured yet.
